# Tomato changes

TOMATO_RDP_PIPELINE_TIMING=1 enables aggregate per-second processing, pixel
extraction and output-wait timings, plus one initial codec identifier. It is off
by default and contains only counters and durations, never stream contents.

The `graphics-h264` feature supplies the bundled OpenH264 EGFX decoder. Software
AVC420 is explicitly opt-in via ConfigBuilder::with_graphics_h264: paired dense
text measurements regressed on the test CPU. Default connections retain Java's
V10 AVC_DISABLED/V8 lossless negotiation and do not instantiate that decoder. A live
decoder advertises V8.1 AVC420 with V8 fallback; unavailable decoders keep the
previous V10 AVC_DISABLED/V8 capabilities. AVC444 is never claimed. Complete
compositor frames are published immediately after protocol responses rather than
waiting for the legacy bitmap batching timer. Opt-in debug diagnostics report
codec IDs and dimensions, without pixel, clipboard or credential payloads.

Windows CLIPRDR uses a bounded lazy streaming decorator around the native text backend. Local paths, remote streams and cross-session forwarding share typed sources. Native HWND events publish OLE virtual files independently of GPU paints. Locks retain immutable snapshots and their generation; late responses, expired IDs and reconnect ID reuse cannot return replacement-file bytes. Backend recreation resets negotiated state. See docs/rdp-channels.md and the five tomato_file_clipboard tests.

RDP input is selected before another synchronous graphics PDU or presentation tick. Transport arrival timestamps are supplied to ActiveStage so automatic bandwidth detection does not report zero bandwidth due to absent timestamps. This does not preempt a decoder in the middle of a PDU.

Native-pointer sessions expose a bounded 64-message fast-path input lane. One
runtime-owned TLS writer serializes these messages with protocol responses,
independently of the synchronous image decoder; no socket write is interleaved
inside another PDU. Input pauses during reactivation, preserves key/button FIFO
order, and updates anti-idle activity. Protocol response buffers transfer ownership
without a second full copy. Dropping the session cancels its writer. Optional
aggregate dispatch counters contain no coordinates, key contents or credentials;
their scope ends at TLS write completion, not remote display response.

Control producers (including native text/file clipboard notifications) share a
short enqueue sequencer with the fast input lane. A later fast input packet
cannot overtake an already queued control command: its fence completes only
after all response frames generated by that command have finished writing.
The TLS writer continues consuming response requests while a fast packet waits
on its fence, preventing a clipboard/input deadlock. Mouse packets with no
pending control remain independent of decoding. Failed control enqueues do not
publish a fence; resize-triggered reconnect retires that command's sequence and
discards the previous activation's queued input. Raw-sender compatibility exists
only for standalone protocol mocks; RdpClient always builds an ordered sender.
The input module's native writer tests block actual write completion and verify
clipboard-before-Ctrl+V, pause/FIFO, failed enqueue and reconnect boundaries.

The ConfigBuilder accepts an explicit client-info performance flag override,
leaving upstream defaults intact when omitted. Tomato uses Java's disabled
wallpaper/theme/cursor-shadow/settings flags, leaves DISABLE_FULLWINDOWDRAG
unset for live window dragging, and retains font smoothing. This does not
change saved connection files or remote registry/preferences outside the
negotiated session.
# Deferred pipeline diagnostics

Optional pipeline timing keeps only the latest 128 aggregate report lines and
flushes through a buffered writer on session drop. It performs no per-second
stderr writes during decoding. The renderer follows the same bounded approach
with shared ownership so cloning its statistics cannot flush during a frame.
Timing remains disabled by default, and codec transitions use the existing
filtered tracing handler rather than synchronous stderr output.

Lossless V10 graphics negotiation matches Java DrdynvcChannel: AVC_DISABLED
without an extra SMALL_CACHE restriction. The compositor still allocates tiles
on demand, caps bitmap cache data at the standard 100 MB limit, and retains its
256 MiB aggregate budget. Optional AVC420 and V8 fallback capabilities keep their
existing policy. The real TLS/CredSSP/EGFX regression checks the negotiated flags,
so the change is verified on the wire rather than only through a configuration
model. [MS-RDPEGFX bitmap-cache rules](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/windows_protocols/ms-rdpegfx/d1c1540f-9bc7-4344-81e0-3cce6b845f86)
define the 16/100 MB capability distinction; this alone is not proof of improved
physical frame pacing.

ConfigBuilder exposes optional network-characteristics autodetection while
preserving its upstream enabled default. Tomato selects Java's fixed-session
default unless `rdpNetworkAutoDetect` is explicitly enabled in its connection
options; connection files are not rewritten. The connector gates both the
early capability bit and the optional MCS message-channel request. Multitransport
still requests the message channel independently when configured. Detection
handlers and transport-arrival timestamps remain available for opt-in sessions.
